name: Easy CAPI for Meta & Pinterest + GTM
author: suhanduman

sections.description:
Easy Meta CAPI & GTM provides a powerful, all-in-one solution for your server-side tracking needs. It creates a seamless data bridge between your WooCommerce store and both the Meta (Facebook) and Pinterest platforms, while also perfectly integrating Google Tag Manager (GTM).

The core advantage of this plugin is its direct server-side integration. It allows you to leverage the full power of the Conversions API (CAPI) for both Meta and Pinterest without the complexity or cost of setting up a separate cloud platform or a GTM Server Container. We’ve written the server-side code so you don’t have to.

This plugin minimizes data loss from browser-based tracking issues (like ad blockers and ITP) and ensures that your GTM (browser) and CAPI (server) events are fed from the same data source, guaranteeing data consistency and flawless event deduplication across both platforms. You can now control your entire tag management setup from one place, with no need for additional GTM plugins.

Core Features:

  • Dual Conversions API Integration: Go beyond the browser. Send rich, reliable event data directly from your server to both Meta (Facebook) CAPI and Pinterest CAPI.
  • Conflict-Free GTM Injection: Automatically injects the Google Tag Manager container script into your site. This eliminates potential conflicts that can arise from other GTM plugins.
  • Unified Data Layer: Creates a standards-compliant dataLayer for both server-side CAPI events and browser-side GTM events. This provides a perfect foundation for event deduplication across multiple platforms.
  • Advanced Event Tracking: Tracks more than 8 standard e-commerce events, including Purchase, AddToCart, ViewContent, and Search for both Meta and Pinterest.
  • Event Management: Easily enable or disable which events are sent via CAPI directly from the admin panel.
  • Real-time Event Log: A built-in, filterable logging system that records the status (success/failure) of every server-side event sent, which is invaluable for debugging.
  • Performance-Focused: Uses a custom database table for log records to ensure your site’s performance is not affected.
  • Automatic Cleanup: Automatically purges log entries older than 15 days to keep your database lean and fast.

Why is Our Data So Powerful?

The data we send to Meta is one of the richest and highest-quality data sets a standard WordPress installation can send. Here’s why:

  • Comprehensive Event Tracking: You send not just the “Purchase” event, but all the critical steps a customer takes along the path to purchase (Product View, Add to Cart, Search, Register, etc.). This gives Meta a complete picture of the customer journey.
  • Rich Customer Parameters: Instead of simply sending an event “occurred,” we send numerous parameters about the person who performed that event, which Meta can then use to match their identity. This boosts Meta’s “Event Match Quality” score. Critical data we send includes: Email address, phone number, first name, last name, IP address, browser information, Facebook cookies (_fbc and _fbp), and WordPress user ID (all encrypted where appropriate).
  • Reliability (Server-Side): We send data that might otherwise be lost due to ad blockers or browser errors through a secure server channel. This increases data volume and consistency.

In short, we send Meta not just data, but meaningful, actionable, high-quality signals. This high-quality data is the most valuable fuel for Meta’s advertising algorithm, providing you with the following direct benefits:

  • Algorithm Optimization: Meta’s algorithm gains a much clearer understanding of your ideal customer. It learns the common characteristics of not only “buyers,” but also “searchers,” “wishlist-adders,” and “registrants”. This makes it more effective at showing your ads to new potential customers who are likely to exhibit these behaviors.
  • More Powerful Retargeting: You can create much more granular and effective remarketing audiences. For example, a campaign for people who “added items to their wishlist in the last 7 days but didn’t purchase” or discount ads for those who “reached checkout but didn’t complete their purchase”.
  • More Effective Lookalike Audiences: When you tell Meta to “find new people like my customers,” the quality of the source audience is critical. Because your source audience is now much more complete and high-quality, the generated lookalike audiences will be more accurate and high-performing.

External Services

This plugin connects your website to the Meta (Facebook) and Pinterest platforms to send event data via their respective Conversion APIs (CAPI). This functionality is essential for tracking user actions and optimizing advertising campaigns on these platforms.

  • Service Used: Meta Conversion API
  • What it is used for: To send user interaction and e-commerce event data from your server directly to Meta’s servers. This allows for more reliable tracking that is not affected by browser-based issues like ad blockers. The data is used to measure ad performance, optimize ad delivery, and build targeting audiences.
  • Data Sent and When: When a user performs a trackable action on your site (e.g., viewing a product, making a purchase), the plugin sends relevant event data. This data includes event details (like product ID and price) and user parameters to help Meta match the event to a user profile. User parameters can include IP address, browser user agent, email, name, phone number (hashed for privacy), and Facebook-related browser cookies (_fbp, _fbc).
  • Service’s Terms and Policies:
    • Meta Platform Terms: https://developers.facebook.com/terms/
    • Meta Data Policy: https://www.facebook.com/privacy/policy/
    • Meta Business Tools Terms: https://www.facebook.com/legal/businesstools
  • Service Used: Pinterest Conversions API
  • What it is used for: To send user interaction and e-commerce event data from your server directly to Pinterest’s servers. This serves the same purpose as the Meta CAPI: providing more reliable tracking for ad performance measurement, campaign optimization, and audience building.
  • Data Sent and When: The data sent is identical in nature to the data sent to Meta. When a user performs a key action, the plugin sends event details and hashed user parameters (IP address, browser user agent, email, name, phone number) to help Pinterest match the event to a user profile.
  • Service’s Terms and Policies:
    • Pinterest Advertising Guidelines: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/advertising-guidelines
    • Pinterest Developer Terms: https://developers.pinterest.com/terms-of-service/
    • Pinterest Privacy Policy: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/privacy-policy

This plugin also integrates with Google Tag Manager (GTM) by injecting its container script into your website’s header. This allows you to manage and deploy marketing and analytics tags (such as the Meta Pixel and Pinterest Tag for browsers) without modifying the site’s code.

  • Service Used: Google Tag Manager
  • What it is used for: To load a JavaScript container from Google’s servers onto your website. This container then loads other scripts (tags) that you have configured in your GTM account. The plugin itself does not decide what data GTM collects; it only enables the GTM service on your site.
  • Data Sent and When: The plugin sends the GTM Container ID to Google’s servers to request the appropriate script for your site. Once loaded, the GTM script may collect user and site data according to the configuration you have set up in your Google Tag Manager account.
  • Service’s Terms and Policies:
    • Google Tag Manager Terms of Service: https://marketingplatform.google.com/about/analytics/tag-manager/use-policy/
    • Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Recommended GTM Setup

Important: Disable Automatic Event Tracking in Meta

To prevent duplicate events and ensure data accuracy, you must turn off Meta’s automatic event tracking feature. This plugin will handle the sending of all events.

  1. Navigate to Events Manager in your Meta Business Suite.
  2. Select the correct Pixel from your Data Sources.
  3. Go to the Settings tab.
  4. Scroll down to the Event Setup section.
  5. Turn Off the toggle for Track Events Automatically Without Code.

Our plugin prepares all data in a standard dataLayer structure for seamless integration with GTM for both Meta and Pinterest.

GTM Configuration Steps

Step 1: Create Variables

Create the following two variables. These will be used for both Meta and Pinterest tags.

  • Event ID Variable:
    • Name: DLV - event_id
    • Type: Data Layer Variable
    • Variable Name: event_id
  • E-commerce Data Variable:
    • Name: DLV - ecommerce
    • Type: Data Layer Variable
    • Variable Name: ecommerce

Step 2: Create Triggers

Create the following triggers using the “Custom Event” type. These will also be used for both Meta and Pinterest tags.

  • Trigger Name: CE - PageView Meta
    • Event name: page_view_meta
  • Trigger Name: CE - View Item
    • Event name: view_item
  • Trigger Name: CE - Add to Cart
    • Event name: add_to_cart
  • Trigger Name: CE - Begin Checkout
    • Event name: begin_checkout
  • Trigger Name: CE - Purchase
    • Event name: purchase

Step 3: Create Meta & Pinterest Tags

Now, create a tag for each event for both platforms.

A) Meta Tags

Create the following tags using the “Facebook Pixel” template (from the Community Gallery).

  • Tag 1: Meta – PageView

    • Event Name: PageView
    • Object Properties: (Leave Blank)
    • More Settings > Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - PageView Meta

  • Tag 2: Meta – ViewContent

    • Event Name: ViewContent
    • Object Properties: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • More Settings > Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - View Item

  • Tag 3: Meta – AddToCart

    • Event Name: AddToCart
    • Object Properties: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • More Settings > Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - Add to Cart

  • Tag 4: Meta – InitiateCheckout

    • Event Name: InitiateCheckout
    • Object Properties: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • More Settings > Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - Begin Checkout

  • Tag 5: Meta – Purchase

    • Event Name: Purchase
    • Object Properties: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • More Settings > Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - Purchase

B) Pinterest Tags

First, install the “Pinterest Tag” template from the GTM Community Template Gallery. Then, create the following tags.

  • Tag 1: Pinterest – PageView

    • Tag ID: Your Pinterest Tag ID
    • Event to Fire: page_visit
    • Event Data: (Leave Blank)
    • Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - PageView Meta

  • Tag 2: Pinterest – ViewContent

    • Tag ID: Your Pinterest Tag ID
    • Event to Fire: view_category
    • Event Data: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - View Item

  • Tag 3: Pinterest – AddToCart

    • Tag ID: Your Pinterest Tag ID
    • Event to Fire: add_to_cart
    • Event Data: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - Add to Cart

  • Tag 4: Pinterest – InitiateCheckout

    • Tag ID: Your Pinterest Tag ID
    • Event to Fire: checkout
    • Event Data: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - Begin Checkout

  • Tag 5: Pinterest – Purchase

    • Tag ID: Your Pinterest Tag ID
    • Event to Fire: checkout
    • Event Data: {{DLV - ecommerce}}
    • Event ID: {{DLV - event_id}}
    • Trigger: CE - Purchase

After setting up all tags, submit and publish your GTM container.

Our Philosophy: Free, Full-Featured, and Community-Driven

This plugin is completely free and fully functional. There are no hidden “pro” versions or locked features. We believe in providing powerful, accessible tools for the entire WordPress community.

We’re always happy to hear feedback. Got a suggestion? Share it! We’ll consider it as long as the vibes are right and we’re in the mood. If you find this plugin useful and would like to support its continued development, please consider making a donation. Your support helps us dedicate more time to new features and providing top-notch support. Thank you!
sections.installation:
1. Upload the easy-meta-capi folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ menu in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to Meta CAPI & GTM from the main WordPress menu.
  4. Enter your GTM Container ID. This will automatically inject the GTM script into your site.
  5. For the server-side connection, enter your Meta Pixel ID and Access Token.
  6. From the “Event Management” tab, select the events you wish to track and save your settings.
  7. Configure your GTM container as described in the “Recommended GTM Setup” section below.
sections.faq:
Does this plugin replace the Meta Pixel?

This plugin manages both sides of your tracking setup to create a complete, unified system:

  • Server-Side: Our plugin reliably sends rich event data directly to Meta’s servers via the Conversion API (CAPI).
  • Browser-Side: Our plugin injects the GTM container onto your site. You then use the GTM interface to deploy the Meta Pixel and other browser-based tags.

This architecture creates a single source of truth. Your site’s data is pushed to a dataLayer, and because both your CAPI events (sent by our plugin) and your Meta Pixel tag (fired by GTM) use the same event_id, Meta can perfectly merge them.

I saw a different setup on Meta/Pinterest’s official site (using a Server Container). What’s the difference?

Yes, the official documentation from Meta and Pinterest often highlights the setup using a Google Tag Manager Server Container. That method is a powerful alternative for users who do not want to (or cannot) write custom server-side code for their website. It offloads the server-side work to Google’s cloud infrastructure.

Easy Meta CAPI & GTM provides a more direct and cost-effective solution by integrating this server-side logic directly into your WordPress site.

  • We’ve Already Written the Code for You: Our plugin contains all the complex PHP code required to send server-side (CAPI) events to both Meta and Pinterest.
  • No Extra Cloud Costs: The biggest advantage of our plugin’s method is that you do not need to set up or pay for a separate cloud server on platforms like Google Cloud. All processing is handled securely on your own web server.

Therefore, when using our plugin, you only need to manage your browser-side tags in the standard GTM Web Container, as explained in our setup guide. You do not need to set up or use a Server GTM Container.

What plugins are required?

WooCommerce is the only hard requirement. Because our plugin injects the GTM script for you, it is strongly recommended that you disable the e-commerce tracking features of other GTM plugins (like Google Site Kit) to prevent data conflicts. The plugin also provides built-in support for YITH WooCommerce Wishlist and Contact Form 7 (optional).
sections.changelog:
2.3.0

  • Major Feature: Full Pinterest Conversions API (CAPI) and Pixel integration.
  • Improvement: Added a robust AJAX-based tracking method for the ‘AddToCart’ event to ensure it fires correctly with all themes and caching systems.
  • Improvement: Enhanced ‘PageView’ event tracking with a dedicated dataLayer push to ensure perfect deduplication between browser and server events.
  • Improvement: Redesigned the admin panel by merging Meta and Pinterest settings into a unified tab.
  • Improvement: Enhanced the event log to display the platform (Meta/Pinterest) for each successful event.
  • Improvement: Added a manual “Refresh Log” button to the admin panel to bypass caching and view real-time event data.
  • Housekeeping: General code refinements and WordPress standards alignment for repository submission.

2.2.0

  • Improvement: Developments for improved Event Match Quality.

2.1.0

  • Security: Added nonce checks for admin forms to prevent CSRF vulnerabilities.
  • Security: Implemented late escaping for all echoed variables in the admin panel to prevent XSS.
  • Security: Hardened database queries by ensuring all parts of the query are properly prepared.
  • Security: Sanitized all $_SERVER superglobal inputs to prevent potential injection issues.
  • Documentation: Added a required “External Services” section to the readme.txt to disclose the use of the Meta Conversion API.
  • Housekeeping: Bumped version number.

2.0.0

  • Major Feature: Added Google Tag Manager (GTM) container script injection. The plugin is now an all-in-one solution.
  • Major Feature: Unified Data Layer for both CAPI and GTM to enable flawless event deduplication.
  • Improvement: Added a GTM Container ID field to the admin settings.
  • Housekeeping: Updated plugin name and description to reflect new GTM capabilities.

1.8.0

  • Feature: Added first name, last name, and phone hashing (fn, ln, ph) for improved Event Match Quality.

1.7.0

  • Improvement: Enhanced overall security.

1.6.0

  • Improvement: Updated admin panel UI/UX for better usability.

1.5.0

  • Feature: Added Dataset Quality API report submission on Pixel ID change.

1.4.0

  • Feature: Added server-side PageView event tracking.

1.3.0

  • Improvement: Optimized performance of event tracking hooks.

1.2.0

  • Security: Hardened database queries and improved input sanitization.
  • Standardization: Added full translation support and aligned code with WordPress.org best practices.

1.1.0

  • Feature: Added dashboard with event statistics.

1.0.0

  • Initial public release.
